reason: Replace stale PR #739 review-blocker SOR truth after no-live remediation of fail-safe cleanup, authorization freshness, readiness, residue, rollback/readback, and impersonation guards.

operation.summary: After recovering stale #731 review/publication truth for PR #739, the current remediation tightened the live GCP scripts and added no-live guard evidence for the review blockers: mutation authorization now fails closed on expired deadlines, approvals older than 120 minutes, cleanup windows over 30 minutes, and non-service-account impersonation identities; the disposable workload script now has an EXIT cleanup trap, independent deadline reaper, injected post-create failure guard, guest readiness/metadata identity readback, and expanded post-delete zero-residue checks; the foundation apply script now uses service-account impersonation, exact project/subnet/firewall/OS Login/IAM/bucket/logging readbacks, and rollback-on-failure. No new live GCP mutation was run during this remediation; the earlier retained live foundation/workload evidence remains historical evidence only, and any fresh live rerun requires a new unexpired operator authorization packet.
changes: Recovered #731 from the stale PR #739 review/publication state before editing.

Tightened .csdlc/prepared/issues/731/validate-gcp-d1-authorization-packet.sh to require an unexpired cleanup deadline, approved_at_utc when approved, approval age no greater than 120 minutes, cleanup lifetime no greater than 30 minutes, and a service-account impersonation identity.

Tightened .csdlc/prepared/issues/731/run-gcp-d1-disposable-workload-proof.sh to validate authorization before mutation, arm an independent deadline reaper, trap failures after instance creation with cleanup deletion, prove guest readiness and metadata service-account identity, and check forwarding rules, firewall overrides, VM-specific IAM, storage-object, and Terraform-state run-label residue in addition to instances, disks, and addresses.

Tightened .csdlc/prepared/issues/731/run-gcp-d1-foundation-apply-and-readback.sh to obtain Terraform access through --impersonate-service-account, trap failed apply/readback with terraform destroy rollback, and assert exact project metadata, workload service account, firewall denominator, IAM, bucket labels, and logging metric readbacks.

Added .csdlc/prepared/issues/731/validate-gcp-d1-remediation-guards.sh and retained .csdlc/evidence/731/remediation-guards/** proving the new guards without live GCP mutation, including synthetic rejected packets, injected workload cleanup, and injected foundation rollback.
Preserved the historical live GCP evidence directories without overwriting them during no-live mock validation.

validation.purpose: Prove the #731 PR #739 remediation fail-closed guards without live GCP mutation: fresh/expired authorization, 30-minute cleanup cap, service-account impersonation identity, injected workload cleanup, deadline reaper presence, readiness/residue coverage, and injected foundation rollback.
Retain traced no-live remediation guard provenance for the current script state.

follow_ups: A fresh live GCP rerun is not authorized by the expired historical mutation packet; before any new terraform apply or disposable workload creation, produce and validate a fresh operator authorization packet with approval age no greater than 120 minutes and cleanup lifetime no greater than 30 minutes.
The retained earlier live foundation/workload evidence is historical evidence for the prior authorized run, not proof that the new remediation scripts have been executed against live GCP.
